item.title: Who owns the muscles: the Japanese robot-actuator duopoly under siege
item.description: Maya Ito on why actuators are 40-60% of a humanoid and the precision reducer is the real moat — the Harmonic Drive / Nabtesco duopoly, China and Leaderdrive, the quasi-direct-drive design shift, the rare-earth magnet chokepoint, and whether the toll booth holds.

item.title: It's not the mine: the rare-earth magnet chokepoint nobody prices
item.description: Wen Chen on why rare earths are a separation-and-magnet story, not a mining one — the heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium) as the real chokepoint, the April 2025 Chinese licensing regime as a permanent rationing dial rather than a one-off, why only a price floor (not a discovery) makes a Western project bankable, and his skepticism of mine-to-magnet-by-2027 timelines, recycling closing the loop this decade, and rare-earth-free motors.

item.title: The drone-defense complex: real moat or a hope about the budget?
item.description: Sam Calley on what Ukraine actually proved about drone warfare, why the airframe-vs-autonomy moat framing breaks, the rare-earth magnet chokepoint nobody prices, why counter-UAS may be the more durable line item, and where there's no clean trade. v3: two-pass spoken-word script, synthetic same-decode cast, pacing + C2 crispness master.

item.title: NVIDIA's Free Shovel: Is the Moat Moving?
item.description: NVIDIA gave away a tiny, open, edge-ready speech model — Nemotron-3.5 ASR. Host Hotblack Desiato and ex-inference-infrastructure operator Priya Venkataraman work out whether that's a moat defense or a moat on the move — and where semiconductor value actually flows as compute shifts from training to inference: the DeepSeek/Jevons fault line, custom ASICs (Broadcom, Marvell), the HBM memory supercycle, and the TSMC/ASML picks-and-shovels.
